questions.content: A market researcher states that she has 95% confidence that the true average monthly sales of a product lie between USD 170,000 and USD 200,000. Explain this statement correctly.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment Chap 8_Confidence interval.docx

questions.content:
Assume normal populations and construct 95% confidence intervals for the mean for each data set:

Set 1: $1,1,1,1,8,8,8,8$

Set 2: $1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8$

Explain why the intervals differ even though the sets have the same mean and range.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment Chap 8_Confidence interval.docx

questions.content:
The amount of paint in one-gallon cans has known standard deviation $\sigma=0.02$ gallon. A random sample of 50 cans has mean 0.995 gallon.

a. Construct a 99% confidence interval for the population mean.

b. Does the result justify a complaint about cans being short of one gallon?

c. Must the population be normal?

d. Repeat parts a and b using a 95% confidence level.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment Chap 8_Confidence interval.docx

questions.content:
A random sample of 20 greeting cards has mean retail value USD 1.67 and sample standard deviation USD 0.32. Assume a normal population.

a. Construct a 95% confidence interval for the mean value.

b. Explain how the interval can help estimate the total value of an inventory of $N$ cards.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment Chap 8_Confidence interval.docx

questions.content: In a random sample of 100 bank depositors, 30 have more than one account. Construct a 90% confidence interval for the population proportion.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment Chap 8_Confidence interval.docx

questions.content:
An auditor samples 200 health-insurance claims and finds that 80 were paid within two months.

a. Construct a 99% confidence interval for the population proportion paid within two months.

b. If at least 90% are supposed to be paid within two months, what should the auditor report?
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment Chap 8_Confidence interval.docx

questions.content: A survey should estimate mean annual family medical expenses with 95% confidence and margin of error at most USD 50. A pilot study estimates $\sigma=400$ dollars. Find the minimum sample size.

questions.content: What factors affect the width of a confidence interval, and how do they affect it?

Which statement correctly interprets a 96% confidence level?

A. There is a 96% chance that this fixed interval contains the parameter.

B. About 96 out of 100 intervals constructed by this method would contain the fixed parameter.

C. There is a 4% chance that this fixed interval misses the parameter.

D. Both A and C are true.

A random sample of 40 from a population has $\bar x=6.05$ and known $\sigma=2.44$.

a. Construct a 95% confidence interval for $\mu$.

b. Would mild population skewness change the result substantially?

The number of soda cans needed per student is normal with known $\sigma=1.2$. A random sample of 25 students has mean 3.2 cans.

a. Construct a 99% confidence interval for the population mean.

b. If 300 students attend, give a conservative number of cans based on the upper endpoint.

A sample of 20 chickens has mean monthly egg production 20 and sample standard deviation 2.

a. Give a point estimate of the population mean.

b. Explain why a t interval is used and state the assumption.

c. Construct a 95% confidence interval.

d. Is a population mean of 21 plausible? What about 25?

Delivery times (minutes) for 14 randomly selected pizza orders are 22, 15, 18, 30, 12, 31, 18, 15, 23, 13, 19, 25, 17, 32. Assume a normal population.

a. Construct a 95% confidence interval for the mean delivery time.

b. Does the interval support the claim that the mean is less than 25 minutes?

Of 18 UIC students, 10 are definitely not willing to pay for an app, so 8 are willing.

a. Construct a 95% confidence interval for the proportion willing to pay.

b. If development stops whenever the proportion is below 80%, should they continue?

Using the pilot standard deviation $s=6.661$ minutes from the 14 pizza deliveries, how many orders are needed to estimate the mean delivery time with 95% confidence and margin of error at most 5 minutes?

Among 35 employees, 16 prefer shuttle plan A, 11 prefer plan B, and the rest prefer neither.

a. Construct 95% confidence intervals for $p_A$ and $p_B$.

b. How many questionnaires are needed for each proportion to have margin of error at most 0.05 at 95% confidence, using the observed proportions for planning?
What is a critical value, and how is it used to test a hypothesis?
What is a p-value, and how is it used to test a hypothesis?

In a random sample of 2,221 U.S. MBA students, 20% expect to remain at their first job for at least five years. Construct a 95% confidence interval for the population proportion and determine whether it supports a proportion below one-fourth.

A company historically has mean receivables outstanding of 50 days with standard deviation 10 days. A random sample of 25 accounts has mean 54 days and sample standard deviation 8 days. Test $H_0:\mu\le50$ against $H_a:\mu>50$ at $\alpha=0.10$, $0.05$, and $0.01$.

For five one-hour production trials, the number of assemblers $x$ and units produced $y$ were $(1,10),(2,15),(3,30),(4,25),(5,40)$.

a. Does a linear relationship appear plausible?

b. Find the least-squares regression equation.

c. Find the correlation coefficient.

d. Predict production with 6 assemblers.

A sample of 100 students without cars has mean GPA 2.68; a sample of 100 students with cars has mean GPA 2.55. Assume independent populations with known standard deviations $\sigma_1=0.7$ and $\sigma_2=0.6$. Test whether non-car owners have a higher mean GPA at $\alpha=0.05$.

Computer Anxiety Rating Scale scores are summarized as follows, with equal population variances assumed:

| Group | Mean | SD | n |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Male | 40.26 | 13.35 | 100 |
| Female | 36.85 | 9.42 | 72 |

Test at $\alpha=0.05$ whether the population means differ, report the p-value, and state the assumptions.

Bone-marrow microvessel densities were measured before and after transplant for seven patients:

| Patient | Before | After |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 158 | 284 |
| 2 | 189 | 214 |
| 3 | 202 | 101 |
| 4 | 353 | 227 |
| 5 | 416 | 290 |
| 6 | 426 | 176 |
| 7 | 441 | 290 |

Let $d=$ before $-$ after. Test at $\alpha=0.05$ whether mean density is higher before treatment, report the p-value, and give a 95% confidence interval for the mean difference.

A report gives a mean systolic-blood-pressure reduction of 24 mmHg with margin of error 4 mmHg at 95% confidence.

a. Find the lower endpoint.

b. If $\sigma=9$ mmHg, find the minimum sample size for margin of error less than 2 mmHg.
questions.source: ROTEL Statistical Problem Sets in WeBWorK — 8.1-8.2 Problem 1 — https://rotel.pressbooks.pub/statsproblemsets/chapter/8-1-8-2-confidence-intervals/

questions.content:
A random sample of 30 used-car transactions has mean sale price USD 2,000, and the population standard deviation is known to be USD 300.

a. Find the 99% confidence interval for the population mean.

b. Interpret it correctly.

questions.content: Prize amounts for 15 television quiz-show winners (dollars) are 43,460; 38,213; 42,876; 38,921; 36,709; 26,735; 35,472; 31,319; 42,833; 27,159; 32,799; 39,271; 44,016; 28,191; 37,087. With unknown population standard deviation, construct a 94% confidence interval for the mean prize.
